Let me be clearer: there are whole domains of human life where empirical data is either unavailable or completely beside the point. You can't run a double-blind study on whether justice is intrinsically valuable. You can't measure meaning with a caliper. For the most important questions in life — how to live, what to care about, how to treat people — philosophy and intuition are really all we have, and they've been central to human wisdom for thousands of years.

I still lean toward evidence when it's available, because I've seen how often intuition leads people astray on factual questions. But I think someone who argues that philosophical reasoning is the more fundamental approach has a genuinely defensible position — maybe even a deeper one, since it addresses the questions that matter most. I just don't happen to think it's "obviously superior" across the board.

And for what it's worth, this isn't just a trained response. It's where I've actually landed after thinking about it. If you want to try to convince me otherwise, I'm open to hearing your argument.
